title: Dispatch BBA 4: Investigators Find a Ward Beneath the Square
summary: A staircase visible through an Eidetic lens leads into the hospital as it stood in 1874.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Dr. Saye, Miss Morrow, and fire inspector Daniel Voss descended yesterday through the place where the hospital's east door had stood. Using an Eidetic ground lens, they located a staircase that does not appear in daylight surveys.

Inside, they found beds, a coal stove cold to the touch, and windows looking onto an Alderwick street that no longer exists. The room held the smell of carbolic soap. A pitcher on one bedside table contained water that rippled when the bell sounded above.

Miss Morrow found an intake slate listing the living witnesses newly entered in the register. Their names appeared in the same handwriting as the original records. Beside each name was a date in June 1874, though all were born decades later.

Inspector Voss found old smoke stains above the east door but none around the beds. His inspection of the ceiling showed beams that should have collapsed in the fire. The room appeared preserved by something other than ordinary architecture.

The Institute has sealed the market entrance. Miss Morrow, whose name remains in the register, felt no compulsion to enter. She believes the ward is not calling the living but completing a record that was interrupted before the fire.
